LLM auditresponse for ipscan:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a minimal launcher script for the ipscan package. It simply invokes `java` to run the ipscan JAR file located at `/usr/share/java/ipscan/ipscan*.jar`, passing through all command-line arguments (`"$@"`). There is no network activity, no file system manipulation beyond launching the application, no obfuscated code, no use of dangerous commands (eval, curl, wget, base64 decoding of blobs, etc.), and no deviation from standard packaging practices for a Java application launcher.

The script is a typical wrapper that allows users to invoke the installed application from the command line. Its behavior is entirely consistent with what one would expect from a wrapper around a pre-installed JAR file.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Simple Java launcher script for ipscan, no security concerns.</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for build.gradle.patch:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This file is a git diff patch showing the removal of two package task definitions (`deb` and `rpm`) from a `packageTask('linux64')` block in a build.gradle file. The changes simply strip out Debian and RPM package format declarations for the linux64 target. There are no network requests, no downloads, no obfuscated code, no eval/base64 usage, and no suspicious file operations. The `'` entities are merely HTML-encoded single quotes and pose no threat. The modifications are consistent with normal AUR package maintenance — restructuring supported package formats or removing obsolete ones. No code executes at a distance, no data is exfiltrated, and no backdoors or reverse shells are present. The diff is inert and serves only packaging-housekeeping purposes.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Patch removes deb/rpm package tasks from linux64 build — benign packaging change
</summary>
</security_assessment>
